title: The 1996 Porsche 911 Turbo: Legacy and Performance
youtube_title: Why the 1996 Porsche 911 Turbo Commands $300K Today 🔥

scenes.headline: $110K -> $300K
scenes.narration: Originally priced at $110,000, this one now commands about $300,000, an appreciation rate reflecting its status and rarity.

scenes.headline: Wide Rear Fenders
scenes.narration: This iconic model features wide rear fender flares, accommodating larger wheels essential for its enhanced performance.

scenes.headline: Signature Spoiler
scenes.narration: The distinctive rear spoiler is a hallmark of the 911 Turbo, not just for style but critical for downforce at high speeds.

scenes.headline: 3.6L Twin-Turbo
scenes.narration: The 3.6-liter twin-turbo flat-six engine generates 400 horsepower and 398 lb-ft of torque, with an air-to-air intercooler prominently displayed.

scenes.headline: Classic Gauges
scenes.narration: Inside, the car showcases vintage circular gauges with orange pointers, reinforcing its classic performance cockpit feel.

scenes.headline: AWD
scenes.narration: The 993 Turbo introduced all-wheel drive to the 911, improving traction and stability, a technological leap for its time.

scenes.headline: Kills Bugs Fast Ad
scenes.narration: Arena Red Metallic became iconic due to the famous 'Kills Bugs Fast' advertising campaign, solidifying the 993 Turbo's legendary status.

scenes.headline: Unique Engine Cooling
scenes.narration: The engine cover's distinctive slats boost cooling for its renowned air-cooled engine, a beloved feature among enthusiasts.

scenes.headline: Legacy Question
scenes.narration: With all these features and its increasing value, is the 1996 911 Turbo a collector's dream or an enthusiast's best drive?

script: Originally priced at $110,000, this one now commands about $300,000, an appreciation rate reflecting its status and rarity. This iconic model features wide rear fender flares, accommodating larger wheels essential for its enhanced performance. The distinctive rear spoiler is a hallmark of the 911 Turbo, not just for style but critical for downforce at high speeds. The 3.6-liter twin-turbo flat-six engine generates 400 horsepower and 398 lb-ft of torque, with an air-to-air intercooler prominently displayed. Inside, the car showcases vintage circular gauges with orange pointers, reinforcing its classic performance cockpit feel. The 993 Turbo introduced all-wheel drive to the 911, improving traction and stability, a technological leap for its time. Arena Red Metallic became iconic due to the famous 'Kills Bugs Fast' advertising campaign, solidifying the 993 Turbo's legendary status. The engine cover's distinctive slats boost cooling for its renowned air-cooled engine, a beloved feature among enthusiasts. With all these features and its increasing value, is the 1996 911 Turbo a collector's dream or an enthusiast's best drive?

sections.Highlights: THIS… is a 1996 Porsche 911 Turbo, finished in Arena Red Metallic with a black interior. This 911 Turbo is owned by journalist and Cars & Bids founder Doug DeMuro, and associated videos are viewable below. This Porsche is equipped with a 6-speed manual transmission, and the odometer currently displays approximately 62,800 miles. This 993 is offered with a clean Carfax vehicle history report, and it has reportedly been registered in California since new. According to the window sticker provided in the gallery, notable factory equipment includes 18-inch Turbo Twist wheels, a limited-slip differential, a sunroof, supple leather upholstery, power-adjustable front seats, and air conditioning. Notable modifications reported by the seller are limited to a Porsche Classic Communication Management (PCCM) head unit. Documentation of maintenance and repairs performed is extensive and reportedly dates back to new. Recent highlights include a $24,470 service in February 2026 that included replacing the valve covers, timing chain covers, crankshaft seal, turbo oil feed lines, and more, as detailed by documentation in the gallery. The 993-generation 911 Turbo, introduced in 1995, was the first 911 Turbo with all-wheel drive, providing enhanced traction and stability. Its twin-turbocharged flat-6 engine, distinctive wide-body design, and status as the final air-cooled Porsche have made it a favorite among Porsche enthusiasts -- and Arena Red Metallic remains one of the most famous 993 Turbo colors thanks to the iconic "Kills Bugs Fast" advertisement. Power comes from a 3.6-liter twin-turbocharged flat-6, rated at 400 horsepower and 398 lb-ft of torque. Power is sent to all four wheels via a 6-speed manual transmission.
sections.Equipment: A window sticker is provided in the photo gallery, and a partial list of notable equipment reported by the seller includes: 18-inch Turbo Twist wheels Xenon headlights Power-operated sunroof Rear wiper Supple leather upholstery Power-adjustable front seats Air conditioning Cruise control
sections.Seller Notes: The seller reports that some touch-up paintwork has been performed on forward-facing surfaces at some point in the past, and a full-body paint protection film and a ceramic coating have since been applied to this 911 Turbo.
